errors.english: this refers to the cause of cognition, and it is connected to the object of observation
errors.why: The gloss says 'from which cause' means 'from the indicating (jñāpaka) [cause]' and is construed with the root-text verb 'is observed'; it does not mean a cause of cognition or an object of observation.

errors.english: No matter which word it depends on, the meaning is extracted from that cause.
errors.why: This is a grammatical gloss: in relation to the word 'which' (yad), the correlative 'from that cause' is to be supplied; it is not 'no matter which word'.

errors.english: One must infer this because a certain result is seen at all times.
errors.why: The sentences from 'Even if any particular state of wind...' to 'because it has a specific cooperating cause' are all the content of the anticipated objection, but the English presents them as the commentator's own assertion.

errors.english: The response to this is the phrase just as smoke where no fire is seen.
errors.why: The statement 'if another cause is imagined, smoke too would not be established as fire-caused' is itself the reply that the root phrase gives; it is not a statement that the root phrase then responds to.

errors.english: raising a doubt one or two words at page break
errors.why: The Tibetan says 'not so' rejects the doubt (the verb 'refutes' comes on the next side); 'raising a doubt one or two words at page break' is a garbled artifact.

fix.find: raising a doubt one or two words at page break

note: The broad argument (habituation, not humours, explains differences in passions) comes through, but the grammatical glosses are garbled, the objection is merged with the reply, and the side ends in a leaked artifact.

errors.english: a practitioner achieves the result of a mantra through a specific application
errors.why: Here 'special' qualifies the practitioner (a special practitioner obtains the mantra's fruit), which sets up the Brahmin vs. śūdra point; the English moves it onto the application.

note: A sound rendering of the argument against the efficacy of mantras; it has only a small misplacement.

errors.english: Likewise, it is impossible for them to possess number, because both number and "possession" are quality-entities
errors.why: ལྡན་པ here is the Vaiśeṣika quality of conjunction (saṃyoga); the text says number and conjunction are both impossible for the six categories, since both are qualities and so reside only in substances.

fix.find: Likewise, it is impossible for them to possess number, because both number and "possession" are quality-entities
fix.replace: Likewise, number and conjunction (saṃyoga) are also impossible for them, because both of these are qualities

errors.english: it refers to things like a palace or a garland
errors.why: The example is 'a row of palaces' (a collective expression), not a palace and a garland.

fix.find: it refers to things like a palace or a garland
fix.replace: it includes expressions like "a row of palaces"

note: The infinite-regress argument on space is handled adequately, but the Vaiśeṣika category passage mistranslates the examples and the quality of conjunction.

errors.english: is a plural term used because clarity is desired to be expressed
errors.why: གསལ་བ here is vyakti, the individual instances: the plural is used because the individuals are meant.

fix.find: is a plural term used because clarity is desired to be expressed
fix.replace: is a plural term used because the individual instances (vyakti) are meant

errors.english: the appropriated and the result of appropriation
errors.why: ཉེ་བར་ལེན་པ is upādāna in the sense of material cause; the lamp and its light are the material cause and what arises from it.

fix.find: the appropriated and the result of appropriation
fix.replace: the material cause and what arises from the material cause

errors.english: Since the destroyer does not endure, it endures by itself.
errors.why: The point is that when the destroying cause is absent the thing abides on its own, so a cause of duration is pointless; the English garbles the argument.

errors.english: the mental consciousness that connects
errors.why: This is the rebirth-linking (pratisandhi) mental consciousness, a technical term.

note: The thread of the argument (refuting the support and abiding, the lamp and light analogy) is recognisable, but several technical terms are wrong or flattened.
A faithful and well-structured rendering of the general and specific characteristics of the Truths and the two kinds of seekers of liberation.

errors.english: then it is reasonable to call it a collection that meets in a single object
errors.why: འདུ་བ is the Vaiśeṣika samavāya (inherence), and the expression is ekārthasamavāya, 'inherence in a single object', not a collection.

fix.find: then it is reasonable to call it a collection that meets in a single object
fix.replace: then it is reasonable to call it inherence in a single object (ekārthasamavāya)

note: The refutation of the variegated whole and of sequential superimposition is rendered well overall, but 'inherence' is consistently given as 'collection'.

errors.english: For the benefit of others,
errors.why: The verse (continuing སྦྱིན་ from the previous side) says 'making clear the excellence of giving'; 'for the benefit of others' is not in the text.

fix.replace: Making clear the excellence of giving,

errors.english: anyone who is truly manifest as a jewel among men is born into the world of the Sugata One Gone to Bliss
errors.why: The verse says that a certain jewel among men, the Sugata, is born, clearly manifest; the Sugata is the subject, not the world into which 'anyone' is born.

fix.find: anyone who is truly manifest as a jewel among men is born into the world of the Sugata One Gone to Bliss
fix.replace: a certain jewel among men, the Sugata, is born, clearly manifest

errors.english: white and radiant like a mass of camphor light
errors.why: The city is white with the camphor-like mass of light from its mansions (བ་གམ, saudha); the mansions are dropped.

note: The colophon and the opening verses on Sāketa are roughly right, but the first verse line and the Sugata verse are mistranslated.

errors.english: possess an essence of diligence because the benefit of beings is never exhausted

fix.replace: are by nature diligent in order to exhaust what harms beings

errors.english: finders of the elements [note: essential qualities] like yourselves are not easily found
errors.why: འབྱུང་བ here is 'appearance/arising': the appearance of such as you is hard to find; 'elements' and the note are wrong.

fix.find: finders of the elements [note: essential qualities] like yourselves are not easily found
fix.replace: the appearance of ones like yourselves is not easily found

errors.english: Until you have attained it, how could you remain so stable?
errors.why: The rhetorical question is how that state could remain unattained by one of such conduct, which means he will surely attain it.

errors.english:
The wisdom that arises toward them
Depends entirely upon them.
errors.why: The person in whom this understanding arises is the one who serves and relies on the parents.

errors.english: Thus have I heard
errors.why: This is the jātaka formula anuśrūyate ('it is handed down'), not the sūtra opening evaṃ mayā śrutam.

errors.english: (Smriti) mindfulness/scripture
errors.why: Paired with the Vedas, smṛti here is the traditional law literature, not mindfulness.

note: The narrative frame is clear, but the hermit's verses contain a reversal and several misreadings.

errors.why: In this Mūlasarvāstivāda text the Sanskrit term saṅghāvaśeṣa is meant; sanghadisesa is the Pali form.

fix.find: the thirteen (sanghadisesa) rules requiring an assembly of the community

errors.english: This mental resolve is the blessing.
errors.why: བྱིན་གྱིས་བརླབ here is the Vinaya act of mental resolution (adhiṣṭhāna): he should resolve in mind, not 'the blessing'.

note: An accurate account of the five modes of Prātimokṣa recitation and the reciter's and elder's duties, with Pali forms and one Vinaya term to correct.
